newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares close lower as Dow fall takes its toll.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares close lower as Dow fall takes its toll.

text.p: * NZ sharemarket closes lower on moderate turnover
* Offshore investors on sidelines after Dow fall
* Paper stocks ease after strong run
Price movements at the close
LAST CHG * NZSE40 cap index -15.10 at 2,507.21
367 -5 * NZSC cap index +12.79 at 5,211.02
346 -6 * NZMC cap index -0.78 at 1,981.49
382 +1 * Volume NZ$68.5 million Futures -5 at 1289
782 -3 * Other movers - -10
The New Zealand share market closed lower on Thursday following the 120-point slide on Wall Street overnight. Even Telecom shed some ground.
At the finish the NZSE40 Capital index was off 15.10 points at 2,507.21, driven down by falls in most leading issues.

"It was reasonably quiet. It was down about 20 at one point but recovered five points around lunchtime when a bit of buying interest was evident in the leaders," Peter Lynds of brokers ANZ Securities said. "But quite a muted day."
He said paper and forestry products stocks were weaker after a good rise on Wednesday.
Carter Holt Harvey shares were down six cents at NZ$3.66 as were Fletcher Paper at $3.46.
"A lower Dow and people (were) standing on the sidelines a bit just wanting to see what happens with regard to interest rates and the currency here," Lynds said.
Brokers said offshore interest was not as firm as lately and even powerhouse stock Telecom backed off three cents to $7.82.
On the money market short bill rates remained high amid loose monetary conditions mainly driven by a weak dollar, which stayed low during Thursday.
